items.stem: Why would you use a 'repeat 10' loop instead of dragging the same block ten times?

options.text: A loop does the same job with fewer blocks and is easier to change
options.rationale: Correct: loops make repeated actions shorter and easier to edit.

options.text: Loops make the sprite move faster every time
options.rationale: A loop repeats the action; it does not speed it up each time.

options.text: Dragging ten blocks is impossible in Scratch
options.rationale: You can drag ten blocks; a loop is just tidier.

items.explanation: Correct: loops make repeated actions shorter and easier to edit.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO things does a variable let you do in a game? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: a variable can store a changing score.

options.text: Remember how many lives are left
options.rationale: Correct: a variable can store the number of lives.
Backgrounds are set with the stage, not a variable.

options.text: Make the computer run without electricity
options.rationale: Variables store values; they do not power the device.

items.explanation: Correct: a variable can store a changing score.

items.stem: A sprite should bounce when it touches red, but it never bounces. What is the most likely bug?

options.text: The if-block or its condition is wrong, or it is not inside a loop that keeps checking
options.rationale: Correct: the decision must be checked repeatedly and use the right condition.
Scratch can detect colours with the touching-colour block.

options.text: The sprite is too small to bounce
options.rationale: Size does not stop a bounce script from running.

options.text: Red is not allowed in Scratch
options.rationale: Any colour can be used in a condition.

items.explanation: Correct: the decision must be checked repeatedly and use the right condition.
